item.title: TISA opens 8th bank in Mt Hagen
item.description: Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa (right) cutting the ribbon marking the officially operation of TISA Bank in Mt Hagen yesterday November 09th (NBC News) TISA Bank has expanded its banking services into Western Highlands Province, officially opening its 8th branch in Mt Hagen yesterday, November 9, together with its first Automated Teller Machine (ATM) outside of Port Moresby.
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa (right) cutting the ribbon marking the officially operation of TISA Bank in Mt Hagen yesterday November 09th (NBC News)

TISA Bank has expanded its banking services into Western Highlands Province, officially opening its 8th branch in Mt Hagen yesterday, November 9, together with its first Automated Teller Machine (ATM) outside of Port Moresby.

The new branch, located at Wamp Nga Haus is expected to provide greater access to banking services for individuals, teachers, small businesses and communities across the province and the Highlands region.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa, who officially opened the branch, acknowledged TISA’s long contribution to the province and the Highlands region, dating back to its beginnings as a savings and loan society.

Governor Rapa also welcomed TISA’s decision to invest in Mt Hagen, saying the move shows growing confidence in the province’s business environment.

"More businesses are beginning to invest in Western Highlands, and the provincial government will continue working to provide a secure and supportive environment for businesses and financial institutions," stressed Governor Rapa.

Rapa says the provincial government will continue to work alongside TISA and other financial institutions to strengthen economic activities in the province.

TISA Head of Retail Noel Keyala says the bank’s expansion is part of its mission to improve financial inclusion by reaching people who remain underbanked or have no access to formal banking services.

"TISA’s investment in banking services is not simply about new technology, but about making banking more convenient and accessible to Papua New Guineans."

"The bank’s success should be measured not only by the infrastructure it builds, but also by the opportunities it creates the communities it supports and the lasting impact it has on people’s lives," outlines the Head of TISA Retail Mr Keyala.

The Mt Hagen branch will provide full banking services, including deposits and withdrawals, new account openings, Visa debit cards, loans and general banking assistance.

The branch will particularly serve educators, small-to-medium enterprises and everyday customers in Western Highlands and the Highlands region with its customer base of more than 5,000 in the region.

TISA began in 1972 as the Teachers Savings and Loan Society (TSL), established to provide savings and loan services to educators in Papua New Guinea.

Over more than five decades, it grew into the country’s largest savings and loan society and the Pacific’s largest credit union, before transitioning into commercial banking.

TISA was officially granted a commercial banking license by the Bank of Papua New Guinea on October 8, 2024, and became TISA Bank Limited.

Governor Rapa cut the ribbon to the new branch and unveiled the ATM, formally marking the start of TISA’s commercial banking operations in Mt Hagen.

item.title: Four thousand households to benefit from IOM emergency relief supplies
item.description: Disaster relief items ready to be distributed (NBC News) The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is targeting 4,000 households severely affected by natural disasters in Papua New Guinea to benefit from its disaster relief items.
item.content:encoded:
Disaster relief items ready to be distributed (NBC News)

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is targeting 4,000 households severely affected by natural disasters in Papua New Guinea to benefit from its disaster relief items.

IOM is a related organization of the United Nations, working as a leading agency in the field of migration, providing humanitarian assistance, driving solutions for displaced people and facilitating pathways for regular migration.

An IOM delegation paid a visit to Lae warehouse, that's keeping all relief supplies to attend to disaster-stricken areas last week.

IOM's Deputy Regional Director, Diane Epstein, said in an interview that IOM is aware of PNG's catastrophic situation and is depending on its donors to work together, including the Australian Government and the American Government.

Epstein explained that only 4,000 households will be assisted, focusing on the most vulnerable who have suffered from Malia and El Niño.

"The relief items consist of household items like utensils that people will be able to use for cooking, buckets to fetch water, and dignity kits for women that they can use for health and safety purposes," Epstein said.

IOM has already reached out to 1,300 households in five provinces, New Ireland, Bougainville, East New Britain, West New Britain and Milne Bay, where they provided food supplies and WASH kits.

The Highlands region is next on the list, with Hela, Enga and Western Highlands to be visited, where they will receive WASH kits donated by the Australian Government.

Inspections were also carried out to provide proper water and sanitation services to some of the areas.

They were accompanied by the Australian Consulate, Mr. Brenton Kanwosky, during their visit to Lae, where they visited a warehouse for the items, a women's safe house and inspected an old water project that has benefited the Labu Tale people for almost a decade.

item.title: PNG Chiefs sign Laybutt on two-year deal
item.description: The PNG Chiefs have signed Papua New Guinea international Zac Laybutt on a two-year deal starting in 2028. Laybutt will become PNG Chiefs Player #008 at the conclusion of his deal with the Cowboys next season, where he has played 42 NRL games since his debut in 2023.
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Chiefs have signed Papua New Guinea international Zac Laybutt on a two-year deal starting in 2028.

Laybutt will become PNG Chiefs Player #008 at the conclusion of his deal with the Cowboys next season, where he has played 42 NRL games since his debut in 2023.

Having played both wing and centre, Laybutt offers further depth and talent to the club’s outside backs as it continues to build a strong squad for its maiden campaign.

An athletic back who has also kicked goals at club and international level, Laybutt is a proud Kumul with five test appearances following his debut in 2023, where he helped PNG clinch the Pacific Bowl championship over Fiji.

Laybutt has since gone on to play eight tests for the Kumuls, including recent appearances during the 2026 Rugby League World Cup.

“We are delighted to have signed Zac, and his signing is particularly meaningful for us as we build a club that proudly represents PNG,” said PNG Chiefs CEO Lorna McPherson.

She said having Papua New Guinean players like Zac representing the PNG Chiefs will be incredibly important to the country’s identity.

“He can help inspire the next generation of rugby league talent in this country by showing what is possible to achieve in the NRL.

“Zac is a wonderful young man, and we are excited to see him take the next steps in his rugby league career with the PNG Chiefs in 2028 and beyond.” She said.

In addition to Finley Glare, Gairo Voro and Morea Morea – who have all been signed on development contracts for 2028 – Laybutt is the fifth Kumuls representative to sign with the club after Alex Johnston was announced as PNG Chiefs Player #002.

PNG Chiefs General Manager – Football Michael Chammas said, “Zac is a player who understands the significance of what we’re building as a club and the opportunity that lies ahead of him as a player here in PNG,”

Chammas said as a player, he has size, athleticism and versatility to excel in multiple positions, and he has shown already in his career that he can handle the demands and challenges of what it takes to be an NRL player.

PNG Chiefs Coach Willie Peters said he was looking forward to watching Laybutt develop and take the next steps in his rugby league journey with the club.

“Zac is a quality young man who brings a willingness to work hard for the team, and he will join our club with good NRL experience behind him and a bright future ahead of him,” Peters said.

“We believe he will only continue to improve as a player and we’re looking forward to watching him continue to develop with our team in the years ahead.”

item.title: Air Niugini to resume Auckland flights after 26 years
item.description: Air Niugini will resume direct flights to Auckland, New Zealand, after a 26-year absence, with three weekly services between Port Moresby and Auckland starting on November 17, 2026. Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer Alan Milne announced the return of the route in Port Moresby today after receiving International Airline Licence No. 29 from Department of Transport Secretary Matthew Wowoni.
item.content:encoded:
Air Niugini will resume direct flights to Auckland, New Zealand, after a 26-year absence, with three weekly services between Port Moresby and Auckland starting on November 17, 2026.

Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer Alan Milne announced the return of the route in Port Moresby today after receiving International Airline Licence No. 29 from Department of Transport Secretary Matthew Wowoni.

Mr Milne said the licence would allow the national airline to operate direct flights every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

The flights will take approximately five hours and 40 minutes and will initially use Boeing 737-800 aircraft before transitioning to the airline's new Airbus A220-300 fleet.

Under the new schedule, flights will depart Port Moresby at 9.30am on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, arriving in Auckland at 6.30pm local time.

Return flights will leave Auckland at 9am on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, arriving in Port Moresby at midday.

Mr Wowoni said adding New Zealand to Air Niugini's existing Australian and Pacific networks would strengthen trade, tourism and regional connectivity.

"The presentation of this licence represents a significant milestone for Air Niugini and Papua New Guinea as the national airline prepares to recommence services to New Zealand after 26 years. It is an important step in strengthening air connectivity, trade, tourism and people-to-people links between the two countries," Wowoni said.

item.title: Bougainville business partners warned to follow registration rules
item.description: The Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority is warning local and foreign business partners in Bougainville to comply with government requirements before starting business operations. Bougainville Immigration Manager Sylvester Vakore says some business partnerships involving locals and foreign investors have used the names of political leaders, including the President of the Autonomous Bouga
item.content:encoded:
The Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority is warning local and foreign business partners in Bougainville to comply with government requirements before starting business operations.

Bougainville Immigration Manager Sylvester Vakore says some business partnerships involving locals and foreign investors have used the names of political leaders, including the President of the Autonomous Bougainville Government, in attempts to advance their business ventures without following proper procedures.

Mr Vakore identified business registration as a key area of concern, saying local business partners must ensure their businesses are properly registered before commencing operations.

He said the registration process includes obtaining the necessary approvals from the Investment Promotion Authority, Internal Revenue Commission, Bougainville Investment Bureau and, for businesses operating in Buka, the Buka Urban Council.

Mr Vakore said the use of names of political leaders and other prominent individuals did not exempt business operators from complying with the required registration processes.

item.title: West New Britain schools end 2026 academic year early due to drought
item.description: All schools in West New Britain Province have formally ended the 2026 academic year, with classes suspended last Friday, November 6, due to prolonged drought conditions affecting the province. The decision was communicated to school administrations through a circular issued by the Provincial Education Board [PEB], advising schools to suspend classes and send student's home.
item.content:encoded:
All schools in West New Britain Province have formally ended the 2026 academic year, with classes suspended last Friday, November 6, due to prolonged drought conditions affecting the province.

The decision was communicated to school administrations through a circular issued by the Provincial Education Board [PEB], advising schools to suspend classes and send student's home.

Executive Manager for the Provincial Division of Education, Vincent Kalatia, confirmed that the PEB made the decision after schools had been affected by El Niño weather conditions since June this year.

Mr Kalatia said the severity of the drought had made it necessary to bring the academic year to an early close.

However, he clarified that schools wishing to hold their annual speech days or end-of-year class parties would still be allowed to do so after classes had been suspended.

He said school administrations could make their own arrangements for these events.

All teachers in the province have also been advised to begin their holidays early because of the ongoing drought conditions.

item.title: Six contestants vie for Oro’s Miss Bird of Paradise title
item.description: Six young women will compete for the Miss Bird of Paradise Northern [Oro] title when the 2026 pageant is held in Popondetta from November 9 to 14. The pageant will be staged under the theme, “Celebrating Oro’s Culture, Heritage, Leadership and Extraordinary Women.”
item.content:encoded:
Six young women will compete for the Miss Bird of Paradise Northern [Oro] title when the 2026 pageant is held in Popondetta from November 9 to 14.

The pageant will be staged under the theme, “Celebrating Oro’s Culture, Heritage, Leadership and Extraordinary Women.”

The six contestants will represent selected local-level governments [LLGs] across the province.

They are Evangelin Kania and Samantha Setiro from Tufi LLG, Theresha Diannah Orere from Oro Bay LLG, Jacobeth Bainda from Tamata LLG, Marie Louise Joekari from Higaturu LLG, and Patricia Abaija Tagete from Kokoda LLG.

Deputy Chairlady of the 2026 pageant, Kewana Irurapa, said the official program would begin on Monday, November 9, with a launch and float parade through Popondetta town.

The contestants will then take part in various activities throughout the week, leading up to the crowning of Miss Bird of Paradise Northern on Saturday, November 14.

Following the crowning, the winner will travel to Port Moresby with the provincial committee to prepare for the National Miss Bird of Paradise Pageant.

Ms Irurapa thanked the Oro Provincial Government and its administration for funding the event and called on the people of the province to support the pageant and its activities.

item.content:encoded:
Moveave and Kamea tribes in Gulf Province will sign a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on the 14th of this month, November, to end their long-running tribal conflict at Upper Taure, Hinenga, Fish Creek in the Taure Lakekamu Local Level Government.

The date has been set by the Provincial Executive Council, while the venue has been selected to be at Urban Malalaua Local Level Government, Kerema District.

The tribes met for the fourth time on the 31st of October to negotiate the venue and date for the MOA to be signed between the two ethnic groups.

It was revealed that a ceasefire agreement already exists, however it will be amended to capture the current concerns and grievances of both parties before the signing.

President for Taure-Lakekamu LLG, Herbert Pokana, and relatives of those who lost lives during the conflict, asked both parties if they wanted genuine peace and if they were serious about putting the issue to rest once and for all.

Both parties, after sharing their grievances on how the conflict has affected their livelihoods, agreed that they wanted peace.

The conflict reportedly started in September 2024 and has since resulted in loss of lives and several people injured. The ongoing conflict has limited access to basic government services for both communities and disturbed peace within Kerema district.

For the peace process, K300,000 will go to the affected families — K100,000 for each of the three families affected, and K200,000 will be shared between the two tribal groups — K100,000 each to make peace the Melanesian way with food and pigs.

Attending the meeting were community leaders, peace committee members and ward councillors from both parties, the Acting Police Station Commander – Inspector Pius Koma, and the President for Taure-Lakekamu LLG, President Herbert Pokana.
